chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father عليهما السلام, who said:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: O Messenger of Allah, I said to my slave-girl: O fornicator. He said: “Did you see fornication upon her?” She said: No. He said: “Surely, retaliation for her will be taken from you on the Day of Resurrection.”

So she returned to her slave-girl and gave her a whip, then said: Flog me. But the slave-girl refused, so she set her free. Then she came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and informed him, and he said: “Perhaps that may suffice for it.”

key_terms.اجْلِدِينِي: flog me; her request for reciprocal punishment
key_terms.زِنًى: fornication; the act requiring proof before accusation
key_terms.سَيُقَادُ: retaliation or requital will be exacted
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَتْهَا: she emancipated her; she set the slave-girl free
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when rights will be restored

ai.seo_question: What does a hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam teach about falsely accusing someone of zina without proof?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a woman who falsely accused her slave-girl of zina without proof, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله warned that she would be held accountable to her on the Day of Resurrection. Seeking to make amends, she offered herself for punishment and then emancipated the slave-girl, after which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said that this might suffice as expiation.
